summary: Oklahoma is now AGENCY-CONFIRMED, and the answer is clean and favorable. The Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation (Wildlife Diversity Program together with its Law Enforcement Division) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) exempts BOTH the Norway rat and the roof rat (Rattus rattus) from ODWC's import/export permit, its commercial breeder license, and its noncommercial breeder license. Keeping, breeding, and selling or trading roof rats are NOT prohibited and require NO ODWC permit; importing or exporting requires no permit and no health certificate. ODWC treats R. rattus as 'not normally found in the wild' (a non-native species) for purposes of that exemption, which resolves the earlier feral-population ambiguity in the keeper's favor. ODWC recommends standard biosecurity to prevent accidental escapes (never release one). The only open thread is the Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food & Forestry (ODAFF), which ODWC suggested contacting in case it enforces separate rules; that inquiry has been sent.
agency_confirmations: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation (Wildlife Diversity Program and Law Enforcement Division), written reply June 2026: OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) exempts both the Norway rat and the roof rat (Rattus rattus) from ODWC's import/export permit, commercial breeder license, and noncommercial breeder license. Keeping, breeding, and selling or trading roof rats are not prohibited and require no ODWC permit; importing or exporting requires no permit and no health certificate. ODWC considers R. rattus a non-native species 'not normally found in the wild' for purposes of that exemption, and recommends standard biosecurity measures to prevent accidental escape.

keep.why: ODWC confirmed in writing (June 2026) that keeping a roof rat is not prohibited and requires no permit. OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25)'s exemption for 'rats (except those species normally found in the wild)' was confirmed by the agency to cover both Rattus species widely kept in captivity (R. rattus and R. norvegicus): ODWC treats R. rattus as a non-native species 'not normally found in the wild,' so it falls inside the exemption despite scattered semi-naturalized populations. The earlier 'unregulated/unclear' reading is superseded by this agency confirmation.
keep.governing_law: OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) (domesticated-animal exemption, covers Norway rat and roof rat); ODWC written confirmation (June 2026).

breed.why: ODWC confirmed (June 2026) that breeding roof rats requires no permit. OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) exempts the roof rat from ODWC's commercial breeder license AND its noncommercial breeder license. (The native-wildlife breeder statute 4 O.S. §4-107 never applied, R. rattus is non-native, and the Commercial Pet Breeders Act covers dogs/cats only.)
breed.governing_law: OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) (exempts roof rat from commercial AND noncommercial breeder licenses); ODWC confirmation (June 2026).

sell_give.why: ODWC confirmed (June 2026) that selling or trading roof rats is not prohibited and requires no permit. The OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) exemption removes them from ODWC's breeder-license and import/export-permit framework, and no other Oklahoma statute imposes a sale prohibition or permit on captive-bred R. rattus.

transport.why: ODWC confirmed (June 2026) that importing or exporting roof rats requires no ODWC permit, and because of that exemption ODWC does not require a health certificate to accompany these animals. Internal movement of a lawfully held pet is unrestricted. (One open item below: ODAFF, the agriculture department, may have separate animal-movement rules, an inquiry has been sent.) Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25) (exempts roof rat from ODWC import/export permit; no health certificate required); ODWC confirmation (June 2026).

restrictions.summary: ODWC confirmed (June 2026) that no permit or license is required to keep, breed, sell/trade, import, or export a roof rat in Oklahoma, and none of these is prohibited. ODWC recommends standard biosecurity to prevent accidental escape. Never release a roof rat. One open item: the Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food & Forestry may enforce separate rules; an inquiry has been sent at ODWC's suggestion.
steps: Use standard biosecurity (secure caging) to prevent escapes, never release a roof rat
(Pending) Confirm with the Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food & Forestry that no separate agriculture rule applies
restrictions.where_to_file: No ODWC filing required; ODAFF inquiry pending

inquiry_focus: RESOLVED for ODWC (June 2026): roof rats are exempt from all ODWC permits and licenses under OAC 800:25-25-3(a)(25), no permit to keep, breed, sell/trade, or import/export, and no health certificate required. Open item: the Oklahoma Department of Agriculture, Food & Forestry (ODAFF), does it enforce any separate rule on keeping/breeding/selling/importing Rattus? An inquiry was sent June 2026 at ODWC's suggestion.
